chunks: And Ibrāhīm ibn ʿUmar narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

"Lost property is of two kinds: the lost property of the Haram—you announce it for one year; if you find its owner, otherwise you give it in charity. And the lost property outside the Haram—you announce it for one year; if its owner comes, otherwise it is like your own property."

"Among the names of مكة are that it is Makkah, Bakkah, Umm al-Qurā, Umm Ruḥm, and al-Bāssah. When they committed oppression there, it destroyed them—that is, annihilated them—and when they were wronged, they were shown mercy."

key_terms.تَصَدَّقْتَ: you give it away in charity
key_terms.تُعَرِّفُ: you publicly announce and identify it for its owner
key_terms.ٱللُّقَطَةُ: lost property that has been found
key_terms.ٱلْبَاسَّةُ: a name of Makkah indicating that it crushes or destroys oppressors
key_terms.ٱلْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary, here referring to the sanctuary of Makkah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on lost property found in the Haram versus outside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes between the ruling of lost property found within the Haram and that found outside it: the former is to be announced for a year and then given in charity if unclaimed, while the latter may be treated as one's own property after a year if the owner does not appear. It also mentions several names of مكة and describes its sacred character, where oppressors are destroyed and the oppressed are shown mercy.
